labels.label: def:continuous_map_ordinary_locus
questions: DEC-40 applied: y is ordinary iff some open U ∋ y has p⁻¹(U) non-empty and each component of p⁻¹(U) mapped homeomorphically onto U; consequently ord(Y) ⊆ p(X) (GX.ordY_subset_range).

labels.label: rem:ordinary_locii_open_but
findings: Under DEC-40 the restriction ord(X) → ord(Y) is ALWAYS a surjective covering map over a locally connected source (GX.isCoveringMap_surjective_restrict_ordX), connected or not. This proves the positive reading of 'the only obstruction ... is the connectedness of ord(X)' (connected ord(X) ⇒ covering) in a stronger form. The negative reading (a disconnected ord(X) prevents a covering) is FALSE under DEC-40: GX.abs_ordX_not_isPreconnected_covering (x ↦ |x|, ord(X) = ℝ ∖ 0 disconnected, restriction still a surjective covering map). GX.isCoveringMap_restrict_ordX_connected_iff only restates the remark for a connected total space; its docstring now says so.
questions: Does 'covering' in rem:ordinary_locii_open_but (l.844) include a connected total space? If yes, the remark is exactly GX.isCoveringMap_restrict_ordX_connected_iff. If no (DEC-40 as written), the restriction is always a covering and the sentence could read 'the restriction ord(X) → ord(Y) is a covering; it is connected iff ord(X) is'. The row is kept closed because the unconditional statement is stronger than the positive reading; the master may mark it partial until the author answers.

labels.label: lem:spread_partial_covering

hypotheses.paper: Y Hausdorff, locally path-connected, first countable (standing)

findings: Surjectivity of the covering is used for Y₁ ⊆ ord(Y): for a covering map in mathlib's sense (possibly non-surjective) one gets p(X₁) ⊆ ord(Y), X₁ ⊆ ord(X), p⁻¹(Y₁) = X₁ (GX.spread_partial_covering'), and Y₁ ⊆ ord(Y) fails for unitTrue : Unit → Bool, X₁ = Unit, Y₁ = Bool (GX.spread_partial_covering_surjective_needed). Consistent with DEC-40's 'covering = surjective covering map'.

Necessity of portlyness (density) is now witnessed with every other hypothesis of the Lean statement, including T2Space and LocallyConnectedSpace X (even LocPathConnectedSpace, second countable) and X₁ locally connected in X: GX.cex_portlyness_paper.

labels.label: cex:openess
questions: As written under DEC-40: p continuous, a spread, the induced X → p(X) a surjective covering map, ord(Y) = ∅. Also recorded: X₁ = ℝ portly, p(X) not open, ord(X) = ∅.

labels.label: cex:portlyness

hypotheses.paper: item 1: covering X₁ → Y₁ (lemma's hypotheses), X locally path-connected (standing)
hypotheses.note: non-injectivity needs only that the restriction is an open map; x ∉ ord(X) uses LocallyConnectedSpace X

findings: Item 2 is proved as written for the paper's own space, with every listed property (GX.cex_portlyness_paper): the topology generated by the subspace components of X ∩ U (GX.portlyTop) makes the injection a spread (GX.isSpread_portlyι) and is the coarsest such topology (GX.le_portlyTop_of_isSpread: every topology making the injection a spread is finer), so the paper's 'coarsest topology' exists and is this one; X is Hausdorff, second countable, locally path-connected; the inner rays are homeomorphic to ∐_ℕ (0,1); p is a spread; X₁ = Y₁ open, X₁ locally connected in X (GX.IsLocallyConnectedIn), X₁ → Y₁ a homeomorphism; ord(Y) = ord(X) = ∅. Since LocallyConnectedSpace and T2Space hold, the example refutes the density-free form of the Lean lem:spread_partial_covering exactly as the paper intends.

The read-only audit's suggested route (subspace components of X ∩ U are portlyTop-connected) is FALSE for this X: for U = ℝ² ∖ {μu} (u a rational unit vector, 0 < μ < 1) the segment (0,μ)u lies in the subspace closure of the rest of X ∩ U, so X ∩ U is subspace-connected, but the segment is clopen for portlyTop. The proofs avoid this: local path-connectedness from explicit bases (Euclidean balls off the disc, ray segments, truncated cones GX.portlyCone at circle points), then 'spread' from local connectedness. The counterexample to the audit's route is recorded in SCOPE as prose, not formalized.
Item 1 now has a cheap inhabitant (GX.cex_portlyness_fst): p = Prod.fst : ℝ² → ℝ, X₁ = ℝ × {0} (not open), Y₁ = ℝ; X₁ → Y₁ a homeomorphism (surjective covering map) and (0,0) ∉ ord(X), 0 ∉ ord(Y).

hypotheses.note: any maps; only the homeomorphisms and the commutation are used

kb_proposals: A non-instance topology on an existing subtype: define it as a @[reducible] def (class-valued defs must be reducible), then a non-reducible type synonym `def T : Type := S` with `instance : TopologicalSpace T := thatDef`; inside generic-τ proofs `letI := τ` takes priority over the global subtype instance.

EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) at this pin: build points with !₂[a, b]; `EuclideanSpace.norm_single` is deprecated (use `by simp` for ‖single i t‖ = |t|); `(w + v : E) i` needs the type ascription before applying to a coordinate; `fun_prop (disch := (intro; positivity))` handles divisions by 1 + t².

A binder `(τ : TopologicalSpace X)` in a theorem is a LOCAL INSTANCE and overrides the global one everywhere in the statement and proof (e.g. on a subtype): write the other topology explicitly (`@IsPreconnected X instTopologicalSpaceSubtype s`, `@Continuous.continuousOn _ _ τ σ _ s h`) or the elaborator reports 'synthesized τ, inferred instTopologicalSpaceSubtype'.

On a type synonym `def T := S` with its own topology, `connectedComponentIn (F : Set S) x` used where `Set T` is expected elaborates with T's topology; force the intended one with `@connectedComponentIn S _ F x` or `(α := S)`.

unitInterval has no LocallyConnectedSpace instance at this pin: to transport a path through a lemma needing a locally connected domain, compose with `Set.projIcc 0 1 zero_le_one : ℝ → unitInterval` (`projIcc_val` recovers t).

The topology generated by components (generateFrom (spreadBasis p)) receives every continuous map from a locally connected space (GX.continuous_generateFrom_spreadBasis) — the tool to build paths and prove connectedness in such a topology.
